text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bund futures ended slightly lower after M3 monetary data and an Ifo report gave mixed signals on the economy. The futures contract closed above 98.00, however, and traders forecast further gains. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 98.04, down 0.07 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended firmer despite more losses for U.S. T-bonds and a sharp pick-up in M4 money supply growth. Analysts said gilts were supported by a wide spread over Bunds, although they did not expect much narrowing near-term. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 107-15/32, up 01/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - December PIBOR was boosted by a 10 basis point cut in the intervention rate. Bond futures were stuck in their range, finding buyers on dips but capped at 124.00. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 123.90, up 0.06 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets moved higher after early weakness, taking support from the firmer lira and the dollar. Futures largely ignored a 2.6 pct yr/yr rise in July wholesale prices and a 0.2 pct yr/yr rise in July producer prices. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 118.10, up 0.46 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries hovered near lows after midday. Strong housing starts data, technical weakness spurred the drop. Jump in Philly Fed prices paid index keeps bear sentiment. Money was seen parked in the three- to six-month bill sector. An ample minority were still seen betting on the Fed keeping monetary policy steady.The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-16/32, down 18/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.06 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures continued their rally, hitting a 14-month high for a benchmark futures contract, but profit-taking cut some gains by the close. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.12, down 0.28 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Britain sprang a surprise on the market with the launch of a $2.0 billion five-year callable FRN. The issue came after weeks of vague speculation that Britain was planning something big. Other new issue business was sparse and headed by Swiss Bank Corp with a $250 million six-year offering. The EIB asked for 20 billion escudos over 20 years. The World Bank increased a structured lira deal.
